p:cNvPr.descr: PART 1: An image depicting catabolic pathways for methionine, isoleucine, threonine, and valine. At the top is methionine (in a box), which begins with H3C, which bonds right to S, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH (all Cs are pink). CH bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N) and right to COO-. Below this is an arrow pointing down to homocysteine (3 steps). Homocysteine begins with HS, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH (Cs are all pink). CH bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N) and right to COO-. Below this are two arrows pointing down. The first, identified as cystathionine beta-synthase (in blue), has serine joining the arrow. Also to the right is PLP. The next arrow is identified as cystathionine gamma-lyase (in blue). To the right is PLP, and an arrow jets off to cysteine [plus] NH4+. Below this arrow is alpha-ketobutyrate, which begins with C, which bonds left to CH2, which bonds left to H3C. C also double bonds up to O and bonds right to COO-. To the right of alpha-ketobutyrate is threonine (in a box), where H3C, which bonds right to CH, which bonds up to OH and right to CH (all Cs are pink), which bonds up to NH3 (plus is over N), and bonds right to COO-. To the left is an arrow pointing left to alpha-ketobutyrate. This arrow is identified as threonine dehydratase (in blue). Below the arrow is PLP, and it has two arrows jetting off. The first points to H2O, and the second points to NH4+. Below alpha-ketobutyrate is an arrow pointing down to propionyl-CoA. This arrow has alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase (in blue) on the left, and two curved arrows on the right. The first curved arrow points from CoA-SH to CO2. Inside that is the second curved arrow, which points from NAD+ to NADH [plus] H+. Propionyl-CoA begins with C, which double bonds up to O, bonds left to CH2, which bonds left to H3C (all Cs are red). C also bonds right to S-CoA. Below this is an arrow (2 steps), which has another arrow joining it from HCO3 (line over the 3). The arrow points to methylmalonyl-CoA, where C double bonds up to O, bonds right to S-CoA, and left to CH, which bonds up to CH3 and left to –OOC. All Cs are red, except CoA and -OOC. Below this is an arrow pointing down to succinyl-CoA in a pink box. The arrow has methylmalonyl CoA mutase in blue on the left and coenzyme B12 on the right. Succinyl-CoA begins with C, which double bonds up to O, bonds right to S-CoA, and left to CH2, which bonds left to CH2, which bonds left to –OOC. All Cs are red, except CoA and -OOC. To the left of propionyl-CoA is isoleucine (in a box), which begins with H3C bonding to the right to CH2 (Cs are blue), which bonds right to CH, which bonds up to CH3 and right to CH, which bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N) and right to COO-. To the right is an arrow pointing right to propionyl-CoA. Below this arrow another arrow jets out to CO2. Above the arrow is 6 steps, and also an arrow bonding up to acetyl-CoA in a pink box, which begins with C, which bonds left to H3C (in blue). C also double bonds up to O and right to S-CoA.

a:r.a:t: Methionine degradation involves transfer of sulfur to serine, generating cysteine.
The remaining methionine carbon skeleton joins the branched amino acid oxidation pathway to succinyl-CoA.
